1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 18:25. This also occurs in verse 16.

2.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֔ם כִּֽי־אַתֶּ֥ם בָּאִ֖ים אֶל־הָ⁠אָ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and tell them that when they are going to the land of Canaan]

Here, **will fall to you** represents “will be assigned to you by casting lots.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [that will be assigned to you by casting lots]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **inheritance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that you may inherit it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:2. This also occurs in verses 13 and 29.
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:12.

3.note: Yahweh is using **upon the hands of Edom** as a common expression of the culture to mean “alongside the border of Edom.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [along the border of Edom]
See how you translated the similar expression in [20:1](ta:20).

6.note: Yahweh is using **it shall be for you the Great Sea and a border** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the Great Sea and its coast will be your border.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the Great Sea and its coast shall be your border]

11.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking of the hillside along **the Sea of Chinnereth** as if it were the **shoulder** of a person. He means the slope that rises from the shore of the sea. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and reach the slope along the Sea of Chinnereth]

13.note: This means the remaining tribes of Israel who will live on the west side of the Jordan River in the land of Canaan. The tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh had already received their land on the east side of the Jordan River.

14.note: The word **For** indicates that what follows is the reason why Moses said in the previous verse that Yahweh was giving this land to only nine and a half tribes. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before.

In this verse, the words **the Reubenite** and **the Gadite** are singular in form, but they refer to all the descendants of Reuben and all the descendants of Gad as groups. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use plural forms for these words.
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:2.

15.note: Moses is using **from across to the Jordan** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the other side of the Jordan River,” which here is the east side. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on the other side of the Jordan River]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:3.

17.note: Yahweh is using **who will inherit the land for you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “who will divide the land among you as your inheritance.” These men will not receive the land for themselves. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who will distribute the land to you as your inheritance]
See how you translated this name in 11:28.

18.note: Yahweh is using **one leader, one leader from a tribe** as a common expression of the culture to mean “one leader from each tribe.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And one leader from each tribe]

Yahweh is using **to inherit the land** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to divide the land among the Israelites as their inheritance.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to divide the land among the Israelites as their inheritance]

19.note:
# General Information:

This is the list of men who will help divide the land among the tribes.

28.note:
# General Information:

This concludes the list of men who will help divide the land among the tribes.

29.note: The pronoun **These** refers to the men whose names Yahweh has just listed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [These men whose names Yahweh has just listed are the ones whom]

The author is using **to make the sons of Israel inherit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to divide the land among the Israelites as their inheritance.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to distribute to the sons of Israel their portions as an inheritance]
